newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine gov't denies wheat is of poor quality.
newsitem.headline: Argentine gov't denies wheat is of poor quality.

text.p: Argentina denied Thursday there were quality problems with the new wheat crop, saying that complaints from buyers were based on efforts to push prices lower.
"The wheat is very good quality," Patricio Lamarca, an advisor at the Agricultural Secretariat, told Reuters.
But traders said there have been complaints from buyers about the wheat, notably a reduction in flour yield.
One trader said Turkey, Egypt and Brazil have complained about the quality of Bahia Blanco wheat.
Another trader said: "The Brazilians are well informed" about the quality problems, something which has made them ask for upriver wheat from the North of the country.
Lamarca dismissed such talk, saying: "All the (wheat) shipments have been controlled. The buyers continue to buy Argentine wheat.
"Brazil wants to buy cheap wheat. Buyers always want to buy cheap and sellers always want to sell expensive."
The problem, according traders, is the level of sprouted or forage wheat mixed in with good wheat. The amount of poor quality wheat mixed in has had the effect of lowering the falling numbers.

The first trader said exporters are selling shipments that are within the government's guidelines on the amount of poor quality wheat that can be mixed, but suggested buyers where not fully aware of the technical aspects of their purchases.

The government estimated the 1996/97 harvest at 15.2 million tonnes, of which one million tonnes is of poor quality because of heavy rains in December, mainly affecting crops in the south of Buenos Aires province.
